scams.name: Ipoh Old Town Unlicensed-Photographer & 'RM 800 Photo Fee' Pressure
scams.description: Ipoh Old Town's heritage zone — Concubine Lane (Lorong Panglima), the Han Chin Pet Soo frontage, the Kinta Riverfront mural wall, the Birch Memorial Clock Tower — has absorbed the national 'unlicensed street photographer' pressure pattern that went viral in July 2025 after Thai tourists at KLCC were charged more than RM 800 for roadside photos; SAYS 'Unlicensed Photographers At KLCC Fined RM 2,000 Each After Alleged Tourist Scam' (says.com, 2025) is the anchor case, with KL City Hall, police and Immigration issuing compound notices to nearly 30 operators and the federal government publicly confirming NO special permits exist for street-side tourist photography anywhere in Malaysia (Bernama, 2025; NST 'KLCC freelance street photographers fined RM 2,000 each', 2025). The same playbook has migrated to Ipoh's 10,000-visitor-a-day heritage lanes per The Star 'From seedy alley to tourist spot' (thestar.com.my, 2024), with community reports providing 2025 traveller baselines. The 2025 mechanic in Ipoh Old Town: (a) a 'freelance photographer' with DSLR and printed lanyard approaches families, couples or solo tourists near Concubine Lane's rainbow-toast stalls or the Mural Art's Lane wall, offering 'one free photo'; (b) after 2-3 shots, a printed RM 100–RM 300 'package' appears — refusal escalates to RM 500–RM 800 'session fee' with lanyard-waving and claims of 'Perak tourism permit'; (c) costumed 'vintage cheongsam' or 'concubine' impersonators pose for selfies then demand RM 50–RM 200 per frame; (d) vendor-side overlay — shop owners claim 'no photo without RM 50 minimum purchase' and block exit; (e) 'photographer' follows tourists 50 metres refusing to delete photos until paid; (f) 'scan QR to pay RM 80' links to phishing pages per community reports. For travelers: (1) no street-side photographer in Malaysia holds a legal permit — the federal government confirmed this in 2025; you owe them NOTHING for a photo you did not contract in advance; (2) if approached, say firmly 'tidak, terima kasih' and walk — no eye contact, no pose; (3) if photos are taken and a fee demanded, say loudly 'saya nak telefon polis' (I want to call the police) — operators evaporate; (4) for costumed characters, agree a price in writing on your phone BEFORE the photo or refuse; (5) never scan a QR code shown on a stranger's phone — only printed codes on permanent signboards; (6) for genuine heritage photos book Han Chin Pet Soo museum — RM 15 admission includes a guided heritage walk; (7) Ipoh Tourist Police (Jalan Sultan Iskandar) speak English: +60 5-253 5522; scam hotline 997; (8) if paid under duress, report to Majlis Bandaraya Ipoh enforcement +60 5-208 3333 within 24 hours — the KLCC 2025 precedent means authorities take these seriously.
scams.avoidance: No Malaysian street-side photographer holds a legal permit — you owe them nothing Walk past; say 'tidak, terima kasih' and do not make eye contact or pose If fee demanded after photos, say 'saya nak telefon polis' — operators evaporate Agree ALL costumed-character prices in writing BEFORE any photo Book official heritage photos via Han Chin Pet Soo museum (RM 15) Ipoh Tourist Police English: +60 5-253 5522; national scam line 997
scams.location: Concubine Lane (Lorong Panglima), Mural Art's Lane, Kinta Riverfront walk, Birch Memorial Clock Tower, Han Chin Pet Soo / Jalan Bijeh Timah, Jalan Sultan Iskandar heritage row, Ipoh Railway Station forecourt

scams.name: AEON Ipoh Station 18 Mall Distraction-Theft (PRC-Linked Ring)
scams.description: Ipoh's busiest shopping-mall pickpocket ring of 2025 was caught on CCTV at AEON Ipoh Station 18 and Ipoh Parade when two women from the People's Republic of China were arrested mid-operation; The Star CCTV coverage 'CCTV footage confirmed that the women made purchases at a number of the malls' (thestar.com.my, 2025) documents the multi-mall pattern. The suspects were confirmed to have worked AEON Ipoh Station 18, Ipoh Parade and Mydin before the arrest, and additional 2025 community reporting shows mall security is actively monitoring. The 2024-2025 ring mechanic: (a) two or three women (often PRC-Mandarin-speaking, well-dressed, carrying branded shopping bags) target women shoppers at the cashier queue of Cold Storage, AEON supermarket or Mydin — one distracts by 'asking for help with product label translation'; (b) second operator reaches into the victim's open handbag, removes purse or phone, passes it to a third walking past; (c) variant near the food court — operator spills water or drops coins on the table, then 'helps clean up' while lifting a phone left beside a handbag; (d) restroom-corridor variant near Ipoh Parade — victim enters stall, operator reaches over the divider for bag hung on the hook; (e) parking-level variant at AEON Ipoh Station 18 — operator bumps victim loading groceries, apologises profusely while partner lifts wallet from handbag; (f) Smart Local Malaysia 2025 reporting (thesmartlocalmy) documents a single Ipoh-mall victim losing RM 10,000+ in cash and card fraud after a pickpocket incident at a pedestrian crossing near the mall. Community reports provide a baseline on the rising mall-theft pattern. For travelers: (1) carry a crossbody bag with the zipper side facing your body — NEVER an open tote inside any Malaysian mall; (2) keep phone OFF the food-court table — in your zipped bag between uses; (3) at the cashier queue, keep your bag in FRONT of you with one hand on the zipper — the 'translation help' approach is the tell; (4) anyone spilling water or coins near you at a food court is running the distraction — grab your phone and bag FIRST, accept no help; (5) inside restrooms, hook your bag on the INSIDE of the door or hold between knees — never on the back-of-stall hook; (6) at the parking level, load groceries with your handbag strap across your chest, not on the trolley; (7) if pickpocketed, mall security desks at AEON Ipoh Station 18 (Level G customer service) and Ipoh Parade (Ground floor info counter) will pull CCTV and call Balai Polis Ipoh Timur — +60 5-547 2222; (8) block cards immediately via bank app (Maybank, CIMB, Public Bank all have in-app card-freeze); the PDRM scam-reporting hotline is 997 (CCID) and the Ipoh Tourist Police speak English at +60 5-253 5522.
scams.avoidance: Crossbody bag zipper-side to body; NEVER an open tote in malls Phone OFF food-court tables — in zipped bag between uses At cashier, bag in FRONT with hand on zipper; refuse 'translation help' Spilled water/coins nearby = distraction — grab bag & phone FIRST Block cards in-app via Maybank/CIMB; Balai Polis Ipoh Timur +60 5-547 2222
scams.location: AEON Ipoh Station 18 (Jalan Bandar Baru), Ipoh Parade (Jalan Sultan Abdul Jalil), Mydin MITC Ipoh, Cold Storage / AEON supermarket cashier queues, food courts, restroom corridors, mall car parks

scams.name: Ipoh 'Macau Scam' Fake-PDRM Phone Impersonation & Bank-Transfer Extortion
scams.description: The 'Macau scam' — a cold-call impersonation of PDRM officers, Bank Negara officials, customs and couriers — is Malaysia's highest-value fraud category and Ipoh is a 2024-2025 hotspot. The Star 'Ipoh trader loses more than RM 1.2 mil to phone scam' (thestar.com.my, via The Star Online Facebook, 2024-2025) is a locally-anchored loss; The Star 'Clerk loses RM 445,000 to phone scammers posing as authority figures' (thestar.com.my, 2024) documents a Hutan Melintang (Perak) case with identical script. Community first-person reports and long-running community threads document the same scripts, and Malaysian community wikis on identifying scams are a canonical reference. The 2025 mechanic targeting tourists in Ipoh hotels (Weil, M Roof, Kinta Riverfront, Sunway Lost World) and long-stay Airbnbs: (a) cold call in English or Mandarin to the hotel room or mobile — 'this is courier/customs, your parcel from China contains illegal goods'; (b) call is 'transferred' to 'Sergeant Badrul of PDRM Bukit Aman' who cites a fake arrest warrant for money laundering; (c) victim told to stay in the room, not tell anyone, and 'cooperate with the investigation' by transferring savings to a 'Bank Negara safe account' for 'verification'; (d) variant using video call — 'officer' in uniform on WhatsApp with PDRM backdrop demands banking-app screen-share; (e) WhatsApp variant — fake PDRM badge image + case number sent via text, victim pressured to transfer RM 50,000–RM 500,000+ in tranches; (f) tourist-specific hook — 'your hotel check-in triggered an immigration flag, you must clear RM 5,000 bond to a verification account or face deportation' per 2025 community reports. PDRM's official Facebook (pdrmsiaofficial, 2024-2025) confirms over RM 500 million lost to phone scammers in recent years. For travelers: (1) no legitimate Malaysian agency — PDRM, Bank Negara, Immigration, Customs, JPJ — will EVER cold-call you, demand money, ask for bank details, or threaten deportation by phone; (2) if called, HANG UP — do not 'press 9' or stay on the line 'to be transferred'; (3) PDRM will never accept payment by bank transfer; real fines are written, paid at a police station with a serialised receipt; (4) NEVER share bank OTPs, PINs, card numbers or screen-share banking apps — not with 'police', 'hotel front desk calling back' or anyone; (5) if an Ipoh hotel room phone rings and the caller claims authority, put the call on hold, walk to the front desk, and verify in person — real authorities will come to the hotel, they don't phone; (6) call the Malaysian National Scam Response Centre directly: 997 (24/7, English available); verify with PDRM Perak HQ +60 5-208 6222; (7) Ipoh Tourist Police (Jalan Sultan Iskandar) +60 5-253 5522 speaks English; (8) if you have already transferred money, call 997 immediately — the first 24-48 hours is the only window to trace and freeze; block your bank cards in-app (Maybank, CIMB, Public Bank freeze buttons) before calling the bank.
scams.avoidance: NO Malaysian agency will cold-call demanding money or bank details HANG UP — do not 'press 9' or accept call transfers NEVER share OTP, PIN, card numbers or screen-share banking apps Verify in person at hotel front desk if room phone rings Malaysian Scam Hotline 997 (24/7 English); PDRM Perak +60 5-208 6222 If money transferred, call 997 within 24 hours and freeze cards in-app
scams.location: Hotel rooms city-wide (Weil Hotel, M Roof, Kinta Riverfront, Sunway Lost World of Tambun, Ipoh Old Town guesthouses), long-stay Airbnbs, mobile phones with Malaysian SIM cards

scams.name: Concubine Lane (Lorong Panglima) Tourist-Trap Overcharge & Instagram-Trap Vendors
scams.description: Concubine Lane (Lorong Panglima) is Ipoh Old Town's single most-hyped tourist strip — The Star 'From seedy alley to tourist spot' (thestar.com.my, 2024) reports up to 10,000 visitors daily across three heritage lanes and roughly 50 shophouses — and the 2024-2025 pricing drift has turned a historically cheap lane into a 3-5x mark-up food-and-souvenir trap. Long-running community threads document the pattern, with 2025 first-person reports on Old Town pricing fatigue and 2025 traveller baselines providing supporting coverage. The 2025 overcharge pattern: (a) 'hand-pulled old-town white coffee' at RM 12–RM 18 a cup when the authentic Ipoh Old Town kopitiam rate is RM 3.50–RM 6 (Sin Yoon Loong, Nam Heong, Thean Chun just 200 metres away); (b) 'Instagram rainbow cheese toast' RM 20 per slice plus a mandatory RM 8 drink (Star 2024); (c) pomelo and nut stalls — RM 30–RM 60 per bag of mixed nuts that cost RM 10 at Ipoh Parade; (d) costumed 'concubine' selfie-hawkers asking RM 20–RM 50 per photo after posing; (e) 'heritage egg tart' vendors charging RM 8 each when the local Restoran Foh San or Sin Eng Heong price is RM 2.50; (f) weekend-only surcharge — some stalls add 'RM 5 sitting fee' or 'QR-code scan to order' that loads a minimum spend; (g) credit-card surcharge — vendors quoting in cash then adding 5-10% 'bank fee' to card payments, often not disclosed. Community reports from KL show the same playbook in adjacent tourist zones. For travelers: (1) walk ONE block out of Concubine Lane to Jalan Bandar Timah for real Ipoh Old Town kopitiam prices — Sin Yoon Loong, Nam Heong, Thean Chun are RM 3.50–RM 6 for white coffee, RM 3–RM 5 for kaya toast; (2) for egg tarts, Sin Eng Heong (Jalan Mustapha Al-Bakri) and Foh San (Jalan Osborne) are RM 2–RM 3 each; (3) ALWAYS ask price BEFORE ordering at any Concubine Lane stall — the 'bao' (packaged) price is typically posted, the 'special' tourist add-ons are not; (4) refuse any QR-code order menu at a street stall — pay cash and ask for a written receipt; (5) for costumed photos, agree the price in writing (type on your phone, show them, they nod) or skip — expect RM 5–RM 15 per photo at most; (6) card surcharges over 2% should be reported to Bank Negara (bnmlink@bnm.gov.my); (7) the genuine heritage experience is Han Chin Pet Soo museum (Jalan Bijeh Timah) RM 15, advance booking at ipohworld.org — it is far richer than Concubine Lane's lane of Instagram props; (8) save the MBI Tourism hotline +60 5-208 3333 for price-gouging complaints and Tripadvisor 'Incident on first night - Ipoh Forum' community threads for ongoing scam reports near the lane.
scams.avoidance: Walk one block to Jalan Bandar Timah for real kopitiam RM 3.50–RM 6 Sin Eng Heong & Foh San egg tarts RM 2–RM 3 (not RM 8 lane rate) ASK price BEFORE ordering; refuse QR-code menus; pay cash with receipt Agree costumed-photo prices in writing or skip (expect RM 5–RM 15 max) Han Chin Pet Soo museum RM 15 = real heritage experience MBI Tourism hotline +60 5-208 3333; Bank Negara bnmlink@bnm.gov.my for surcharges
scams.location: Concubine Lane (Lorong Panglima), Market Lane, Second Concubine Lane, Jalan Bijeh Timah junction, Ipoh Old Town souvenir row, costumed-character photo spots near Mural Art's Lane

scams.name: Fake Traffic-Police Document-Check & Cash Shakedown in Ipoh
scams.description: Ipoh's fake-traffic-police shakedown pattern produced a landmark 2025 conviction — Malay Mail 'Two men fined RM 5,000 each for impersonating traffic police, demanding money from teens in Ipoh' (malaymail.com, 2025-11-04), New Straits Times 'Two men fined RM 5,000 each for impersonating police' (nst.com.my, 2025), The Star 'Duo fined RM 5,000 each for impersonating cops' (thestar.com.my, 2025) and Bernama 'Two Friends Fined RM 10,000 For Impersonating Traffic Police' (bernama.com, 2025) all cover the same Ipoh Magistrates' Court ruling. The convicted pair stopped victims at 12:38 AM on Jalan Lebuh Bercham Selatan 1 and Tong Seng Street wearing 'uniforms resembling traffic police including cream-striped black trousers', threatened summonses over 'modified motorcycles' and extracted a RM 400 bank transfer; Wong Jiun Wei (24) was caught with a genuine PDRM cap and JSPT boots and fined an additional RM 2,000. Community reports document the reaction. Tripadvisor 'Incident on first night - Ipoh Forum' (tripadvisor.com) is a long-running community thread with a Perth traveller's near-miss involving three men in a grey SUV with a PDRM card but no photo. The 2025 pattern affecting tourists: (a) two men in matching dark-blue or black polo shirts with printed 'PDRM' or 'JSPT' flash approach pedestrians, motorcyclists or cyclists on Old Town side-streets (Jalan Masjid, Jalan Sultan Iskandar, Jalan Bercham); (b) demand to see passport/IC and driving licence, then 'find' an infraction (no helmet, wrong-way one-way, 'modified vehicle'); (c) offer to 'settle on the spot' for RM 200–RM 500 cash instead of RM 2,000+ summons or arrest; (d) variant with a genuine PDRM cap (stolen or bought online) to create authenticity; (e) e-wallet / QR-code payment demand (DuitNow QR) which moves money instantly to a mule account; (f) late-night Old Town bar-exit targeting — tourists leaving Concubine Lane bars after 10 PM singled out. Critically, genuine Malaysian traffic police (JSPT) NEVER accept cash on the spot — all fines are written (Form POL 257) and paid at any police station, balai polis, Pos Malaysia, or via the JPJ/MyBayar Saman app. For travelers: (1) ask politely 'boleh saya lihat warrant card?' (may I see your warrant card?) — genuine PDRM have a laminated photo-ID card; a card without photo is fake per Tripadvisor 2016 community reporting and the 2025 Malay Mail conviction; (2) NEVER pay cash on the spot — say 'saya nak bayar di balai polis' (I want to pay at the police station); genuine officers will accept this; (3) NEVER scan any QR code offered by an officer — real fines are NOT paid by QR to an individual; MyBayar Saman is the only legitimate app; (4) show a laminated photocopy of your passport — never surrender the original; (5) ask for their name, rank, and PDRM ID number and WRITE IT DOWN on your phone in front of them — fake officers bail; (6) if you feel unsafe, say 'saya nak telefon konsulat saya dan 999' (I want to call my consulate and 999) — 999 is the Malaysian police emergency number; (7) Ipoh Tourist Police (Jalan Sultan Iskandar) +60 5-253 5522 speak English; PDRM Perak HQ +60 5-208 6222; (8) if shaken down, file a report at the nearest balai polis within 24 hours for possible refund and prosecution — the November 2025 convictions show Perak courts are actively prosecuting.
scams.avoidance: Ask 'boleh saya lihat warrant card?' — real PDRM have PHOTO-ID card NEVER pay cash on the spot — say 'saya nak bayar di balai polis' NEVER scan a QR code offered by an officer — real fines are not paid this way Show passport photocopy only; write down badge number in front of them Emergency: 999; Ipoh Tourist Police +60 5-253 5522 (English)
scams.location: Jalan Sultan Iskandar, Jalan Masjid Old Town, Jalan Bercham, Jalan Lebuh Bercham Selatan 1, Tong Seng Street, Taman Ipoh Timur Baru, Concubine Lane bar-exit streets late-night, Jalan Sultan Idris Shah hotel row

scams.name: Cave Temple & Gua Tempurung 'Guide / Parking / Donation' Tout Overcharge
scams.description: Ipoh's four flagship cave attractions — Kek Lok Tong, Sam Poh Tong, Perak Tong (all free-entry Buddhist cave temples) and Gua Tempurung (official RM 22 limestone-cave tour) — are 2024-2025 tout zones where unofficial 'guides', 'parking attendants' and 'donation collectors' extract RM 50–RM 200+ from tourists who do not realise entry is free or that official tours are cheap. Tripadvisor 'Entrance fee is not equal to donation - Review of Perak Tong Cave Temple' (tripadvisor.com) documents the pattern; Tripadvisor 'Kek Lok Tong Cave Temple and Zen Gardens' FAQ confirms the temples are free. Community reports and 2025 traveller baselines provide supporting coverage. The 2024-2025 mechanic: (a) at Perak Tong (Jalan Kuala Kangsar), men in yellow safety vests wave tourists into 'VIP parking' for RM 20–RM 50 when the temple's own lot is free and 20 metres further; (b) unofficial 'English-speaking guide' intercepts at the entrance offering '30-min tour' at RM 100–RM 200 per person — the free signage already covers the content; (c) at Sam Poh Tong (Jalan Gopeng), a 'donation collector' with a clipboard demands 'RM 50 maintenance fee' — the temple has a voluntary donation box inside, no fee at entry; (d) at Kek Lok Tong (Gunung Rapat), touts at the pond demand RM 10 per pellet bag for 'fish feeding' (RM 1 elsewhere); (e) at Gua Tempurung (Gopeng, 25 km south), unofficial guides at the car park offer 'full 2.5-hour adventure' at RM 150–RM 250 per person when the official Jabatan Mineral dan Geosains counter charges RM 22 Tour 1 (40-min dry walk) and RM 33–RM 66 for full wet-dry tours with certified guide; (f) 'taxi-tour' combo — a Grab or unofficial driver offers 'all four caves for RM 350' then pockets the touts' commission. Community reports warn about the cave-tout ecosystem. For travelers: (1) Kek Lok Tong, Sam Poh Tong and Perak Tong are ALL FREE — any gate fee or 'mandatory donation' is a scam; give voluntarily into the clearly-marked box inside if you wish; (2) Gua Tempurung's ONLY legitimate ticket counter is the Jabatan Mineral dan Geosains office at the cave entrance — RM 22/33/44/66 per tour level, certified guide included; (3) refuse 'VIP parking' — temples and Gua Tempurung have free official parking 20–50 metres past the touts; (4) refuse unofficial 'guide' intercepts — temples are self-guided with English signage; arrange through Tourism Perak +60 5-255 2772 if needed; (5) decline 'fish-feeding' and 'incense' upsells at the entry; (6) book cave tours via Ipoh Tourist Information Centre or a MOTAC-licensed operator; (7) Grab fares from Ipoh city: Perak Tong RM 15–RM 25, Kek Lok Tong RM 20–RM 30, Gua Tempurung RM 60–RM 80 one-way — never accept off-meter 'combo' quotes; (8) report tout harassment to Tourism Perak +60 5-255 2772 or 999.
scams.avoidance: Kek Lok Tong, Sam Poh Tong, Perak Tong are FREE — any gate fee is a scam Gua Tempurung official counter: RM 22 Tour 1, RM 33–RM 66 full tours Refuse 'VIP parking' — free lots are 20–50 metres past the touts No unofficial 'English guide' — temples are self-guided with English signs Grab flat fare from city: Perak Tong RM 15–RM 25, Gua Tempurung RM 60–RM 80 Tourism Perak +60 5-255 2772; emergency 999
scams.location: Perak Tong (Jalan Kuala Kangsar), Sam Poh Tong (Jalan Gopeng), Kek Lok Tong (Gunung Rapat), Gua Tempurung (Gopeng, 25 km south), Kellie's Castle parking, Tasik Cermin access road, cave-temple car-park touts city-wide
